introduction.text: The Fonte di Anna Perenna is a votive fountain dating to the 4th century BC, dedicated to the Roman goddess Anna Perenna. Discovered in 1999 during construction work, it provides a rare glimpse into the cult practices and magical rituals that continued at the site until the 6th century AD.

history.description: The fountain was constructed in the 4th century BC as part of the cult of the goddess Anna Perenna.
The fountain remained in use until the 6th century AD, when it was abandoned.
The site was excavated and the fountain was discovered in 1999 during the construction of an underground parking lot.

design.description: The fountain is rectangular, built from tuff blocks and bricks, and features an altar on its front façade.

art.description: A Latin inscription on the altar reads "NYMPHIS SACRATIS ANNAE PERENNAE", and the site yielded numerous artifacts including coins, bronze vessels, ceramic bowls, and lead tablets with curses.
